how_to_obtain: Verify per NIST SP 800-53 AU-2 / AU-3 that every read of the PII store is logged with subject, object, timestamp, and source; review the data-store's audit configuration (e.g. PostgreSQL pgaudit, MySQL audit plugin, MongoDB auditLog, AWS CloudTrail data events on S3/RDS/DynamoDB).

Run a benign authenticated SELECT against a PII table and confirm a record appears in the audit sink within the documented latency window — absence proves the trail is off (source: OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet, 'Event Attributes' section).
Cross-check against PCI DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1.1 (all individual access to cardholder data is logged) and CIS Controls v8 Safeguard 8.5 (collect detailed audit logs).
Insecure value (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Audit-log tampering' exposure — without the trail there is nothing for an attacker to tamper with, but the underlying detection gap is the same.

Review the cryptographic inventory: algorithm must be AES-GCM or AES-CCM with key length >= 128 bits, no DES/3DES/RC4/MD5/SHA-1 for confidentiality, no ECB mode (source: OWASP Cryptographic Storage Cheat Sheet, 'Algorithms' section).
Confirm PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.5.1 attestation of strong cryptography with minimum 112-bit effective key strength and a documented crypto-agility plan for weak-cipher retirement.

Inspect the data store's encryption configuration (e.g. `aws rds describe-db-instances --query 'DBInstances[].StorageEncrypted'`, `gcloud kms keys describe`, TDE algorithm in SQL Server `sys.dm_database_encryption_keys`) and confirm AEAD mode.
Enum values 'none' or 'weak' are OR-triggers of the 'Unencrypted PII at rest' exposure; 'strong' is required to satisfy PCI DSS Req 3 and NIST SP 800-53 SC-28 (Protection of Information at Rest).

Verify NIST SP 800-53 AU-9 evidence: audit logs are shipped to an append-only / WORM sink (S3 Object Lock, Azure Blob immutability, GCS Bucket Lock, dedicated SIEM with retention lock), and data-plane admins cannot modify or delete log entries.
Confirm cryptographic integrity: hash-chained / signed log streams (e.g. AWS CloudTrail log file validation via `aws cloudtrail validate-logs`, journald FSS, syslog-ng disk-buffer with HMAC).
Cross-check against PCI DSS v4.0 Req 10.3.2 (audit log files protected from modification) and Req 10.3.4 (file-integrity monitoring on logs).
Insecure value (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Audit-log tampering' exposure — maps to MITRE ATT&CK T1562.008 (Disable or Modify Cloud Logs).

option_name: Audit management restricted to privileged subset (separation of duties)
how_to_obtain: Per NIST SP 800-53 AU-9(4) separation of duties: list the IAM principals with permissions to rotate, delete, or reconfigure the audit-log sink and confirm they are disjoint from the data-plane principals who can read/write PII.

Inspect IAM policies — e.g. `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` against `logs:DeleteLogGroup` / `s3:PutBucketPolicy` on the log bucket; Azure RBAC `Microsoft.Insights/*` role assignments — data-plane admins must NOT hold these.
Review PCI DSS v4.0 Req 10.3.1 (read access to audit logs limited to job-related need) and Req 6.4.2 / 7.2 (separation of duties between development, operations, and audit).
Insecure (false) — same principal can both touch the data and erase the evidence — is an OR-trigger of the 'Audit-log tampering' exposure.

Inspect the backup register: every backup target lists encryption, KMS key, retention, and restore-test cadence (source: NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 Guidelines for Media Sanitization, §4 Media Sanitization Categories).

Run cloud-provider checks: `aws rds describe-db-snapshots --query 'DBSnapshots[].Encrypted'`, `aws ec2 describe-snapshots --owner-ids self --query 'Snapshots[].Encrypted'`, `aws s3api get-bucket-encryption` on the backup bucket — every entry must be true.
Confirm PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.5.1 covers backup media (the requirement is media-agnostic) and Req 9.4.1 (media containing cardholder data physically secured).
Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Unencrypted PII at rest' exposure — backups are the most common forgotten cleartext copy that re-exposes data even when the primary store is encrypted.

option_name: Bulk export anomaly monitoring and alerting
how_to_obtain: Review the monitoring stack for volumetric anomaly rules on the PII store: row-count thresholds, byte-volume baselines, query-cardinality alerts (e.g. CloudWatch metric alarms on `BytesDownloaded` for S3, Datadog DB query-volume monitors, Splunk anomaly detection on SELECT row counts).

Run a synthetic bulk-export test: SELECT 10x the normal page size, or perform an S3 ListObjects + bulk GetObject, and confirm an alert fires within the documented SLA (source: OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet, 'Event Monitoring' section).
Cross-check against CIS Controls v8 Safeguard 13.3 (Deploy a Network Intrusion Detection Solution) and Safeguard 8.11 (Conduct Audit Log Reviews).
Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Bulk exfiltration without DLP or egress monitoring' exposure — maps to MITRE ATT&CK T1030 (Data Transfer Size Limits) detection gap.

option_name: DLP / egress controls on PII outbound paths
how_to_obtain: Inspect the DLP coverage matrix: every outbound channel (HTTP API, SQL export, email, cloud-storage upload, removable media) has detection patterns for PII/PAN/health-data with block-or-quarantine action (source: CIS Controls v8 Safeguard 3.13 Deploy a Data Loss Prevention Solution).

Run a synthetic exfil test: upload a marked test PII payload (canary records, marked-credit-card test BIN) to an external web service and confirm the egress is blocked or alerts (source: MITRE ATT&CK T1567 Exfiltration Over Web Service).
Inspect product configuration: e.g. Symantec / Forcepoint DLP rule sets, Google Cloud DLP InspectJobs, AWS Macie sensitive-data findings; Netskope / Zscaler CASB egress rules.

Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Bulk exfiltration without DLP or egress monitoring' exposure — covers MITRE ATT&CK T1567, T1567.002 (Exfiltration to Cloud Storage), and T1537 (Transfer Data to Cloud Account).

Architecture review confirms encryption at rest on every store of customer data (DB, object store, backups, search index, message-queue persistence, caches) — ciphers AES-128-GCM/CCM or stronger (source: OWASP Cryptographic Storage Cheat Sheet, 'Storing the Cryptographic Material').
Confirm PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.5.1 evidence that PAN is rendered unreadable anywhere stored — via strong cryptography, one-way hash, truncation, or tokenization.

Per-platform check: `aws s3api get-bucket-encryption --bucket <pii-bucket>`, `aws rds describe-db-instances --query 'DBInstances[?StorageEncrypted==\`false\`]'`, `gcloud sql instances describe`, MongoDB `db.serverStatus().encryption`; cross-reference NIST SP 800-53 SC-28 (Protection of Information at Rest).
Insecure (false) is the primary OR-trigger of the 'Unencrypted PII at rest' exposure — maps to CWE-311 and MITRE ATT&CK T1213 (Data from Information Repositories).

Review the schema and ORM/data-access layer: list each sensitive column (PAN, SSN, national ID, full DoB) and the protection applied — truncation, one-way hash (with appropriate salt/pepper), tokenization (vault token), field-level encryption (e.g. AWS KMS envelope, MongoDB CSFLE), or pseudonymization (source: NIST SP 800-188 De-Identifying Government Datasets, §4 De-Identification Techniques).
Confirm PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.5.1 strong-crypto, Req 3.4.1 PAN-rendered-unreadable when stored, and Req 3.4 PAN masked when displayed (max first-six / last-four).

Inspect tokenization-vault configuration (e.g. HashiCorp Vault Transit / Transform engine, TokenEx, Skyflow): confirm the production data-store holds only tokens, with format-preserving or random tokenization documented.
Enum value 'none' is an OR-trigger of the 'Unprotected sensitive fields (no masking/tokenization)' exposure — equivalent to CWE-200 record-level exposure.

Inspect the record-of-processing: every cross-border transfer to a non-adequacy country must be covered by GDPR Article 46 safeguards — Standard Contractual Clauses (2021 Commission set), Binding Corporate Rules, or equivalent (source: GDPR Articles 44–49).
Confirm a documented Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) post-Schrems II (CJEU C-311/18) for each transfer, addressing third-country surveillance law and supplementary technical measures.
Sample one active vendor / sub-processor that processes PII outside the controller's region and pull the signed SCC plus TIA — absence on any transfer means the attestation is false.
Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Data residency / sovereignty violation' exposure.
Network test: `curl -sI https://<host> | grep -i strict-transport-security` — expect `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload` or similar per RFC 6797.
Confirm submission to the browser HSTS preload list via https://hstspreload.org/?domain=<host> for top-level domains carrying PII (source: OWASP HTTP Strict Transport Security Cheat Sheet).
Inspect reverse-proxy / load-balancer config (e.g. nginx `add_header Strict-Transport-Security`, AWS ALB rule, Cloudflare HSTS toggle) and confirm `max-age` >= 31536000 (1 year).
Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Cleartext or downgraded transport of PII' exposure — without HSTS a sslstrip-style downgrade puts PII on the wire in clear (MITRE ATT&CK T1557).

Inspect KMS rotation configuration: `aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id <id>` must report `KeyRotationEnabled: true`; Azure Key Vault `az keyvault key rotation-policy show`; GCP `gcloud kms keys describe --format='get(rotationPeriod)'`.
Confirm PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.7.4 attestation: cryptographic keys rotated at the end of the defined cryptoperiod, per NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 guidance (typical: 1 year for DEKs, 2 years for KEKs).
Cross-check against OWASP Key Management Cheat Sheet 'Key Rotation' section: documented rotation policy AND evidence of actual rotation events in the KMS audit log.
Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Weak key management (keys co-located, unrotated, no HSM/KMS)' exposure.

Review the key-generation procedure: KEK/DEK must be generated as full-entropy random material by an HSM/KMS, not derived from a human-chosen passphrase fed through PBKDF2/scrypt/Argon2 (source: OWASP Key Management Cheat Sheet, 'Key Generation' section).
Inspect config files, environment variables, and secret-manager entries for patterns like `ENCRYPTION_PASSWORD`, `KEY_PASSPHRASE`, `MASTER_PASSWORD` — any such derivation is the insecure value.

Confirm PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.6.1.2 (cryptographic keys distributed securely) and Req 3.7.6 (split knowledge / dual control of cleartext keying material) — passphrase-derived keys typically violate split-knowledge.
Insecure (true) is an OR-trigger of the 'Weak key management (keys co-located, unrotated, no HSM/KMS)' exposure.

Verify key inventory shows DEKs wrapped by KEKs in a KMS/HSM (e.g. AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault Premium, HashiCorp Vault Transit, Thales Luna HSM); KEKs never appear in application config or source (source: OWASP Key Management Cheat Sheet).
Confirm PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.6 attestation: key-management procedures cover generation, distribution, storage, rotation, retirement; Req 3.7 covers split-knowledge / dual-control.

Scan source repos and container images for hard-coded key material: `gitleaks detect`, `trufflehog filesystem .` — must return zero high-confidence findings for encryption keys (mitigates CWE-798 Use of Hard-coded Credentials).
Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Weak key management (keys co-located, unrotated, no HSM/KMS)' exposure — common in early-stage stacks that ship encryption-key material in `.env` files.

Architecture review: key-storage blast radius must be disjoint from ciphertext blast radius — KEK in KMS (separate IAM, separate region replica) with wrapped DEKs alongside ciphertext is acceptable; raw DEK in the same DB row or volume is not (source: OWASP Key Management Cheat Sheet, 'Key Storage' section).
Inspect backups: a backup that contains both ciphertext AND the raw key collapses the control — confirm KMS keys are NOT included in DB snapshots.
Confirm PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.6.1.3: access to cryptographic keys restricted to the fewest number of custodians necessary, separated from access to the data.
Insecure (true) is an OR-trigger of the 'Weak key management (keys co-located, unrotated, no HSM/KMS)' exposure.

Entitlement review shows access to personal-data tables / buckets granted by named role with documented business need; entitlements reviewed at least annually (source: CIS Controls v8 Safeguard 3.3 Configure Data Access Control Lists, Safeguard 6.8 Define and Maintain Role-Based Access Control).
Confirm PCI DSS v4.0 Req 7.2.1 access control system covers all components, Req 7.2.4 (review user access at least once every six months), Req 7.2.5 (manage application / service accounts).
Inspect IAM: `aws iam list-policies --scope Local` for the PII data store; flag any `*:*` or `<service>:*` on the PII resource. Cross-reference NIST SP 800-53 AC-6 (Least Privilege).
Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Over-broad access to PII stores' exposure — maps to MITRE ATT&CK T1213 (Data from Information Repositories).
Confirm PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.5.1 attestation: PAN is rendered unreadable anywhere it is stored, by one of strong cryptography, one-way hash (full PAN), truncation (first 6 / last 4), or tokenization.
Sample the PII data store: SELECT a sample row and confirm the PAN column is not in cleartext — it contains a token, a truncated value, or ciphertext.
Inspect any analytics export, replication target, search index, and log sink — PCI DSS Req 3.5.1 applies everywhere PAN appears, not only the primary store.
Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Unprotected sensitive fields (no masking/tokenization)' exposure — by definition a PCI DSS Req 3.5 finding.

option_name: PII excluded from logs and telemetry
how_to_obtain: Log analysis: `grep -E '[0-9]{13,19}|[\w.-]+@[\w.-]+\.\w+|password=|authorization: bearer' <log_sample>` — should produce no hits; logging framework has redaction filters on known sensitive field names (source: OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet, 'Data to exclude' section).
Code review confirms structured logging with explicit, allow-listed fields; debug logs disabled in production; CWE-532 (Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File) controls in place.
Inspect APM / distributed-tracing config (Datadog, New Relic, Honeycomb) for span-attribute denylists / scrubbers on `http.request.body`, `db.statement`, `user.email`.
Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'PII leakage into logs and telemetry' exposure — logs are typically retained longer and more broadly accessible than the primary data store.

Architecture review: identify the at-rest layers protecting PII — disk/volume (LUKS, BitLocker, EBS volume encryption) AND/OR application/column/tablespace encryption (TDE, MongoDB CSFLE, application envelope encryption); if ONLY the disk layer is present, the attestation is true (insecure).

Confirm the threat model recognises that volume crypto is transparent to a live OS — a compromised application, DB account, or host reads cleartext (source: OWASP Cryptographic Storage Cheat Sheet, 'Storage' guidance).

Cross-check PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.5.1.2: where disk-level encryption is used on non-removable media for PAN, additional controls must apply (or a layered control such as column-level encryption is recommended).
Insecure (true) is an OR-trigger of the 'Unencrypted PII at rest' exposure — even where `encrypted_at_rest` is true, single-layer disk crypto fails the threat model for live-host compromise.

Inventory check: pull the regions of every PII-bearing store — primary DB, replicas, snapshots, search indexes, caches, log sinks — via `aws ec2 describe-regions`, `aws s3api get-bucket-location`, `aws rds describe-db-instances --query '[].[DBInstanceIdentifier,AvailabilityZone]'`, GCP `gcloud asset search-all-resources`, Azure Resource Graph.

Cross-reference against the contract / regulator-approved region list (e.g. EEA + adequacy-decision countries for EU PII); any residency outside the list is insecure (source: GDPR Articles 44–49 + Schrems II CJEU C-311/18).
Confirm DR replicas, ad-hoc operational copies, and downstream processor locations are scoped — the dossier flags these as common silent escapes.
Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Data residency / sovereignty violation' exposure — maps to MITRE ATT&CK T1537 (Transfer Data to Cloud Account) in the cross-account / region exfil sense.

Retention schedule is keyed by data class; automated purge job evidence (cron history, scheduled-task logs, lifecycle policy via `aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration`); backups also rolled within the retention window (source: NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 Guidelines for Media Sanitization).
Confirm PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.2.1: cardholder data storage is minimized; data exceeding retention is securely destroyed; Req 3.1 sets the data-retention and disposal policy requirement.
Cross-check GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) storage-limitation: documented purpose-linked retention period; sample DSAR fulfilment evidence to confirm purge actually runs.
Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Indefinite retention and unsafe deletion' exposure.

Inspect database-level controls: PostgreSQL row-security policies (`SELECT * FROM pg_policies`), MySQL views with `WHERE` tenancy clauses, SQL Server Row-Level Security predicates, Snowflake row-access policies + dynamic-data-masking policies, BigQuery row-level access policies + column-level access tags.

Confirm PCI DSS v4.0 Req 7.2.1 (access control covers all components and accounts) and Req 7.2.5.1 (application / system accounts have access restricted to that necessary); CIS Controls v8 Safeguard 3.3 (Configure Data Access Control Lists).
Sample test: connect as a low-privilege role / service-account and SELECT — confirm the result excludes other tenants' rows and that PII columns return masked / null values.
Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Over-broad access to PII stores' exposure — table-level grants without finer scope mean one compromised analyst reads everyone.

Inspect the logging framework's redaction config: e.g. Logback `replace` patterns, log4j2 `ReplaceConverter`, Winston / Pino redact arrays, Serilog destructuring policies — must scrub known sensitive field names (`password`, `authorization`, `cookie`, `api_key`, card-number patterns) before sinks (source: OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet, 'Data to exclude' section).

Confirm coverage extends across centralised sinks: Splunk / Elastic / Loki forwarders apply props.conf / pipeline filters; distributed-tracing spans (OpenTelemetry) have processors stripping sensitive attributes.
Log analysis sample: `grep -iE 'authorization: bearer|password=|secret=|api[_-]?key=' <production_log_sample>` — should produce no hits over a 24-hour sample window (CWE-532 mitigation).
Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'PII leakage into logs and telemetry' exposure — together with `pii_excluded_from_logs` covers CWE-532 end-to-end.

Confirm retention-end deletion applies NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 sanitization (Clear / Purge / Destroy) matched to media risk, OR crypto-shredding (KMS key destruction makes ciphertext unrecoverable) across primary stores AND backups.

Inspect KMS-key lifecycle for crypto-shred evidence: `aws kms schedule-key-deletion` audit history; key-rotation + decommission policy documented per OWASP Key Management Cheat Sheet 'Key Destruction'.
Confirm PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.2.1 (data exceeding retention rendered unrecoverable) and Req 9.4.7 (electronic media destroyed when no longer needed).
Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Indefinite retention and unsafe deletion' exposure — 'soft' logical deletes do not satisfy this.

Per the schema, every high-sensitivity field (PAN, SSN, government ID, biometric) is protected by at least one of: truncation, one-way hash, tokenization, field-level encryption, or pseudonymization (source: NIST SP 800-188 De-Identifying Government Datasets + PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.3–3.5).
Sample query as a low-privilege role: confirm PII fields return masked / tokenized / encrypted values, not plaintext.

Inspect application code paths that handle sensitive fields: tokenization-vault calls, format-preserving encryption wrappers, hash-with-pepper helpers — confirm no code path persists cleartext alongside the protected form.
Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Unprotected sensitive fields (no masking/tokenization)' exposure — a PCI DSS Req 3.3 / 3.5 audit finding.

option_name: Shared admin / service accounts to PII store
how_to_obtain: Per PCI DSS v4.0 Req 8.2.1: all access is identified to an individual user — generic / shared / group accounts to the PII data store are prohibited; confirm via `SELECT usename FROM pg_user`, MySQL `mysql.user`, AWS IAM users on the DB resource, MongoDB `db.getUsers()`.

Cross-check NIST SP 800-53 IA-2 (Identification and Authentication — Organizational Users): each user uniquely identified before access; CIS Controls v8 Safeguard 5.4 (Restrict Administrator Privileges to Dedicated Administrator Accounts).
Interview the on-call rota: confirm break-glass / emergency-access credentials are per-person (vaulted with checkout audit), not a shared root password.
Insecure (true) is an OR-trigger of the 'Over-broad access to PII stores' exposure — one credential compromise yields the whole dataset and queries cannot be attributed.

Review the deletion implementation: a soft-delete (tombstone column, `deleted_at` flag, status='inactive') that leaves the underlying row, plus its appearance in backups and replicas, is the insecure value (source: dossier 'retention_and_deletion_policy' surface).
Sample test: 'delete' a test PII record via the application, then connect as DB admin and confirm whether the row is still SELECTable; check whether the most recent backup still contains the row.

Confirm GDPR Art. 17 (Right to Erasure) compliance: subject-erasure runbook must propagate to primary, replicas, search indexes, analytics warehouses, AND backups within the retention rollover window.
Insecure (true) is an OR-trigger of the 'Indefinite retention and unsafe deletion' exposure — Marriott / H&M-class finding pattern.

Per CIS Controls v8 Safeguards 3.1 / 3.2 / 3.7 (Establish and Maintain a Data Inventory, Manage Data Inventory, Establish and Maintain a Data Classification Scheme): data inventory covers structured + unstructured stores, primary + backups, with classification labels; reviewed >= annually.
Cross-check GDPR Art. 30 records-of-processing: each processing activity names every storage destination including geographic location; sub-processor list is current.

Inspect inventory tooling: AWS Macie / GCP Cloud DLP / Azure Purview discovery scans for PII across accounts; reconcile findings against the documented inventory — undiscovered storage means the attestation is false.
Insecure (false) is an OR-trigger of the 'Data residency / sovereignty violation' exposure — you cannot prove residency you do not know.

option_name: TLS-only transport for PII (no cleartext fallback)
how_to_obtain: Network test: `openssl s_client -connect <host>:<port> -tls1_2` succeeds AND a plaintext attempt (`curl http://<host>:<port>/`) is refused / redirected with 301 to HTTPS (source: CIS Controls v8 Safeguard 3.10 Encrypt Sensitive Data in Transit).

Inventory of every flow touching personal data documents TLS termination + minimum version — east-west AND north-south, internal service-to-service AND service-to-DB (source: GDPR Article 32(1)(a) appropriate-measure record).

Inspect listener configuration: nginx / Envoy / HAProxy have no plain HTTP `listen` on PII-bearing endpoints; DB clients enforce `sslmode=verify-full` (PostgreSQL) / `--ssl-mode=VERIFY_IDENTITY` (MySQL); message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ) accept TLS-only listeners. Cross-reference NIST SP 800-53 SC-8 (Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity).
Insecure (false) is the primary OR-trigger of the 'Cleartext or downgraded transport of PII' exposure — maps to CWE-319 and MITRE ATT&CK T1557 (Adversary-in-the-Middle).

Network test: `nmap --script ssl-enum-ciphers -p <port> <host>` OR `testssl.sh --severity HIGH <host>:<port>` — output must show TLS 1.2 / TLS 1.3 only, no SSLv2/v3/TLS 1.0/TLS 1.1, no RC4/3DES/EXPORT/NULL ciphers (source: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet).
Confirm PCI DSS v4.0 Req 4.2.1 strong cryptography and security protocols for in-transit cardholder data — TLS 1.2 minimum; weak ciphers (including those marked WEAK by IETF) disabled.

Inspect proxy / load-balancer / TLS-terminator policy: AWS ALB `SecurityPolicy` is `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06` or stricter; Cloudflare SSL/TLS minimum version is 1.2; nginx `ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;` and `ssl_ciphers` restricted to Mozilla 'intermediate' or 'modern' profile.
Insecure (true) is an OR-trigger of the 'Cleartext or downgraded transport of PII' exposure — an active MITM can negotiate the downgraded session and read PII (MITRE ATT&CK T1557).
